title: Self-validating Terraform module for EKS control plane with health sentinels and safe migrations
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a production-ready Terraform module to provision Redwood Private EKS control planes with built-in, automated health sentinels and migration safety checks. The module should provide declarative inputs for upgrade policies, automated pre/post upgrade validation hooks, and a lightweight health sentinel subsystem that signals success/failure to the orchestration pipeline. This work reduces manual upgrade toil and decreases blast radius during control plane changes for VPC/private customers.
background: We currently manage EKS control plane provisioning via a collection of Terraform modules and ad-hoc scripts. Upgrades and control-plane changes require manual validation, runbook-driven checks, and frequent on-call involvement. Drift and partial upgrades have caused incidents in past rollouts. This ticket consolidates several patterns into a single self-validating module that can be used by Private deployments and by the EKS provisioning operator.
goals: Provide a single Terraform module that provisions EKS control plane resources and a paired health sentinel (CloudWatch + Lambda) that validates key control-plane properties after provisioning or upgrades.
Support pre-upgrade and post-upgrade validation hooks that can be executed from CI/CD or the provisioner operator.
Expose inputs for safe rollout policies (canary percentage, pause durations, automatic rollback triggers).
Emit structured metrics and logs consumable by Console dashboards and incident runbooks.
Be idempotent and follow Terraform best practices for lifecycle and drift detection.
non_goals: Replace the provisioner operator — this module is intended to be consumable by it, not to replace it.
Implement full-scale cluster autoscaling or worker node lifecycle management (outside control plane scope).
Ship a complex UI — observability hooks will surface to Console but UI work is separate.
acceptance_criteria: Module can provision an EKS control plane and associated sentinel resources in a test VPC using Terraform apply without manual steps.
Pre-upgrade validation step will fail fast when control-plane invariants are violated and surface a clear reason via logs and metric tags.
Post-upgrade sentinel will report success within configurable timeout; failures trigger a documented rollback path in the runbook.
Module inputs are documented in the README and example usage exists in infra-private/examples/ with a minimal CI pipeline integration example.
E2E automated test runs in CI demonstrating a canary upgrade (10% control planes) and rollback on induced failure.
implementation_steps: Design schema for module inputs/outputs and publish README with examples.
Implement Terraform resources: eks cluster (control-plane config), IAM roles, SSM parameters (for sentinel signals), SNS topic for events.
Create lightweight sentinel Lambda (Python) that runs validation checks against control-plane endpoints and reports to CloudWatch metrics and SSM param signal.
Add optional local-exec/remote-exec hooks for invoking pre/post upgrade validators from CI or operator.
Wire structured CloudWatch metrics and logs; add tags for environment, release, and control-plane-id for correlation in Console.
Author CI job in infra-private/.github/workflows/ that runs an upgrade scenario and verifies sentinel behavior.
Add integration tests that intentionally inject a failure (tainted resource) to validate rollback and alerting behavior.
Document operational runbook with steps for manual rollback, diagnostics, and debugging sentinel failures.
testing_plan: Unit test Terraform module with terraform-compliance and tflint in CI.
CI E2E tests: provision a test cluster, run sentinel checks, simulate upgrade, validate post-upgrade sentinel reports.
Chaos test: inject API server certificate rotation failure and assert sentinel catches it and signals failure.
Load test: ensure sentinel Lambda scales/handles checks for up to 50 concurrent control-plane validations without rate limiting.
Manual oncall dry run: runbook walkthrough with SRE to validate diagnostics and rollback paths.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sentinel false positives during transient API hiccups. Mitigation: implement configurable retry/backoff and require N consecutive failures before marking an upgrade as failed.
Risk: Additional IAM surface area increases blast radius. Mitigation: least-privilege IAM for Lambda and restrict SNS/SSM usage to module-scoped resources.
Risk: Terraform state conflicts when operator and manual runs overlap. Mitigation: document recommended locking (DynamoDB) and add optional lifecycle ignore_changes where appropriate.
Risk: Cold-start / rate limits on Lambda cause delayed signals. Mitigation: use provisioned concurrency for production critical control planes and allow signal timeout tuning.
decisions: Use SSM Parameter Store for simple success/failure signaling rather than S3 to avoid eventual-consistency edge cases — trade-off: small per-parameter cost vs simpler semantics.
Implement sentinel as a Lambda invoked on schedule and on-demand (via SNS) so both CI-driven and periodic checks are supported.
Prefer CloudWatch metrics + tags for Console integration rather than a custom telemetry endpoint to reduce operational overhead.
Rollout policy model: support percentage-based canaries at Terraform invocation level (operator will compute targets); we will not encode complex rollout orchestration inside Terraform.
